plans.note: Section 21 has a mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a consequential-damages exclusion with direct-damage clarifications, and an Excluded Claims definition covering confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnity, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud and IP. Check 21.3 exclusion list and 21.4 savings language; 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit liability.

Vendor IP indemnity in 20.1 and conduct-based indemnity in 20.2; Customer's reciprocal indemnity in 20.3 is narrow with carve-backs. Confirm procedure (20.4) and infringement remedies/refund basis (20.5, cross-referenced by 9.3).

12.3 expressly preserves Customer's freedom to develop, buy or build and disclaims non-compete/MFN/no-hire commitments. Cross-check against the exclusivity language in the first 2.2 to see whether any residual restriction on Customer's business exists; if only exclusivity, handle under EXCLUSIVITY.

The first Section 2.2 makes Vendor the sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the term — a direct hit on this rule, in tension with 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and 12.3 (no exclusivity acknowledged). Note the duplicate 2.2 numbering (sec-2.2 vs sec-2.2-2).

The first Section 7.2 obliges Customer to give Vendor terms no less favourable than its best terms to any other technology supplier — an MFN running against us. Contrast with 12.3's disclaimer of any MFN commitment; note duplicate 7.2 numbering (sec-7.2 vs sec-7.2-2, the invoicing clause).

12.4 binds Customer for eighteen months post-termination, covers anyone employed by Vendor at any time during the term, extends to 'engage', and has no general-advertising carve-out. Reconcile with 12.3's statement that no no-hire commitment was made.

Section 9 contains only for-cause, insolvency and incident-based termination (9.1–9.3, 9.5); no convenience right for Customer appears anywhere, and 8.1/8.2 fix a three-year term with renewals. Note 27.3 (force-majeure exit) and 10.2 (refund of prepaid Fees) as adjacent mechanics before concluding the rule is missing.

8.2 auto-renews Order Forms for twelve months on a one-hundred-eighty-day notice window — assess against the playbook's acceptable window. 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and three percent with ninety days' notice, which is favourable and should be noted rather than flagged.

28.1 selects New York law with CISG excluded; 28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts with an injunctive-relief carve-out; 28.3 adds an executive-escalation step. Appears within the accepted list — verify no arbitration elsewhere.

24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent; 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment and competitor transfers; 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating or repricing on our change of control. 13.3 cross-references Section 24 for licence transfers.

14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP; 14.2 assigns Deliverables on creation subject to payment; 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology with the 13.2 perpetual licence; 14.4 avoids joint ownership and limits feedback use. Check 15.1's no-training/no-sale restriction and the definitions in 1.3, 1.4 and 1.8 for leakage.

13.1 extends access to Affiliates and contractors for internal business purposes; 13.2 grants a perpetual, irrevocable paid-up licence for delivered Vendor Technology; 13.3 limits revocation/suspension to uncured material breach after notice. 13.4 restrictions should be checked as reasonable.

22.1 permits Vendor audits at any time without notice with remote access to Customer systems — squarely contrary to the rule; 22.2 and 22.3 provide cost-shifting, scope limits and confidentiality that partially mitigate. Section 23 (records/assurance) may hold related language.

7.6 imposes USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages on Customer for any dependency delay — a penalty running against us with no cap or cure. Consider interaction with the liability cap in 21.1 and the dispute-withholding right in 7.3.

19.1–19.3 give services, conformity, malicious-code and compliance warranties; 19.2 sets a ninety-day Deliverable warranty with hosted Services conforming throughout the term; 19.4 provides re-perform/repair/replace with refund fallback and is expressly non-exclusive for key claims. Acceptance remedies in 6.1–6.2 are adjacent.

18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O and USD 5,000,000 cyber coverage for the term plus one year; 18.2 covers insurer quality, certificates, cancellation notice and non-limitation of liability. Compare limits to playbook minimums.

2.1 expressly disclaims any minimum quantity or purchase commitment and confirms non-ordering is not a breach; 7.1 bars unstated minimum-use charges and 12.3 disclaims minimum-volume commitments. Favourable to us — confirm the exclusivity in the first 2.2 does not create a de facto commitment (handled under EXCLUSIVITY).

11.1 gives up to six months' transition assistance at expiring rates for any termination reason; 11.2 requires data return within thirty days in machine-readable format with no fee-dispute hostage-taking; 11.3 covers certified deletion. 10.1–10.2 and 16.5 supply related post-termination mechanics.
